title: Louis on modern paintings at the Louvre
summary: Armstrong told Young the Russians put the modern paintings up to confuse Americans.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: -- he told me one day -- I never forgot this. He said -- it was in Paris, and some people had just took us down to Louvre, you know, to see all --

So he told me when he came out, he said, Trummy, you see all them pictures with the eyes and all coming out? He talking about modernistic paintings, you know. He said, did you see all those things? I said yeah. He said, what did you notice about them? I said, well, it's real modern, Louis, you know. He said, let me tell you something. You know who put those things up? I said no. He said, the Russians put them things out to confuse the Americans.

He said, if you see a horse, you know that's a horse, don't you? If you see a rose, you know -- I couldn't believe it, what he was talking. I told Billy Kyle Collins, and he laid on the floor laughing. I couldn't believe it. This guy -- laughed about two weeks until my stomach hurt me. I didn't know whether he was putting me on or whether he really, really believed it, but I couldn't believe it. I just couldn't -- these things -- he used to come on right out of the clear sky with, things like you just couldn't believe.
